sources.label: Transport for NSW — Getting to and from Sydney Airport
Transport for NSW — Opal fares & travel

blocks.text: Bondi sits about 7 km east of the Sydney CBD and roughly 14 km from the airport by road, and from either you're realistically 30 to 60 minutes away. The catch that trips up almost every visitor isn't the distance — it's that there's no train station at the beach itself.

items.label: Nearest station
items.value: Bondi Junction (~3 km uphill, then a bus)

blocks.title: There is no Bondi Beach train station
blocks.text: The name catches people out. The closest station is Bondi Junction — the eastern terminus of the T4 Eastern Suburbs & Illawarra line — about 3 km up the hill. From the interchange upstairs you take a 333, 380 or another Bondi Beach bus down Bondi Road to Campbell Parade, getting off around the Lamrock Avenue stop for the main stretch of sand. It's roughly a 10-minute ride.
Door to door from around Sydney
From the CBD, Circular Quay and the Opera House

The easy one. The 333 is a limited-stops bus that runs from Alfred Street at Circular Quay straight through the city to the beach, so you can skip the train entirely and stay on one bus — it's the direct city service to Bondi. Allow roughly 30 to 50 minutes; after the Opera House you can go from harbour to surf without working out a single connection. Check the Transport for NSW Trip Planner for the current departure stop and times before you set off.

A taxi or rideshare is usually 25 to 45 minutes over the roughly 14 km, though the Eastern Distributor bunches up in peak hour — leave a buffer if a flight is involved. On public transport you've got two sensible options: take the T8 Airport & South Line into the city and change to a T4 train for Bondi Junction, or skip the train fee with the Route 350 bus, which runs from the Domestic Terminal to Bondi Junction via Mascot, Maroubra and Coogee. Either way you finish with a beach bus down to Campbell Parade.

blocks.title: The airport station access fee
blocks.text: Both airport train stations charge a station access fee on top of the normal Opal fare — it's a well-known sting. The Route 350 bus from the terminal avoids it, which is often why I point people to the bus.
From Manly and the Northern Beaches

Sydney's two most famous beaches sit on opposite sides of the harbour, so this is the long one — comfortably over an hour by public transport. My favourite route is also the most scenic: the Manly ferry to Circular Quay, then the 333 out to Bondi, which turns a slog into one of the best half-days in the city. Driving across the bridge or through the tunnel is genuinely unpredictable, so I'd budget 45 to 75 minutes.

Tap on with a contactless card or your phone — no physical Opal card needed. One tap covers the train, a second the connecting bus, and the daily and Sunday fare caps apply just the same. Only child, concession and senior fares still need a physical Opal card.

You can drive, but I rarely recommend it. Street parking around Campbell Parade is metered, time-limited and fiercely contested on any warm weekend — nine times out of ten the train-and-bus combo beats circling for a space. Sort out the Bondi Junction connection, tap on, and the distance takes care of itself.

items.q: Is there a train station at Bondi Beach?
items.a: No. The nearest is Bondi Junction, the eastern terminus of the T4 line, about 3 km up the hill. From there a 333, 380 or another Bondi Beach bus runs down to Campbell Parade in around 10 minutes.

items.q: How far is Bondi Beach from Sydney city centre?
items.a: About 7 km east of the CBD. The 333 express runs from Circular Quay straight to the beach, or take a T4 train to Bondi Junction and change to a bus — usually 30 to 50 minutes.

items.q: How do I get from Sydney Airport to Bondi Beach?
items.a: It's roughly 14 km by road. A taxi or rideshare is quickest at 25 to 45 minutes. By public transport, take the T8 line into the city and change for Bondi Junction, or catch the Route 350 bus from the Domestic Terminal to Bondi Junction to avoid the airport station access fee — then a beach bus to Campbell Parade.

items.q: What's the best way to get from Manly to Bondi?
items.a: The Manly ferry to Circular Quay, then the 333 to Bondi — scenic and simple. Allow well over an hour, since you cross the harbour either way.
